free_tier.stated: No free tier. The international line's entry plan is 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 30 GB SSD, 1 TB of monthly traffic, a 200 Mbps port and 1 dedicated IPv4, at VND 220,000 a month or VND 1,900,000 a year, with VAT added at checkout (the page shows VND 242,000 due today for the monthly cycle); the vendor's own forum post gives USD 59 a year at the regular price and 30% off with coupon LOWEND30.
free_tier.notes: the entry plan on the Germany page is VPS DE-4; the same 4 GB entry shape was read on the Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, UK, Australia, France, Italy and Netherlands pages, and the USA pages carry 3 TB of traffic instead of 1 TB

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine, not stored bytes; the vendor states a 7-day money-back guarantee subject to its refund policy
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the running process and its disk

egress.terms: 1 TB of monthly traffic on the entry plan over a 200 Mbps port; the vendor's forum post states the same figure, and the cart page for the USA entry plan states 3 TB

interface_detail: a management panel with start, stop, reboot, password reset and reinstall, and a VNC console; no API was read
tooling: panel and VNC console; the vendor lists Linux and Windows images; no API or CLI was read
chaining: USD 59 a year buys 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM and 30 GB of SSD with 1 TB of monthly traffic in 18+ locations, against VN-1A's 1 vCPU, 1 GB and 20 GB in Hanoi for USD 18.50 a year, so VN-1A is the cheaper entry point and this line is the one to take when 4 GB of RAM is the floor.

identity_cost.detail: the sign-up form marks an email address, a password, a first and last name, an address, a country and a phone number as required, plus a captcha; no card is asked for at sign-up, and the payment methods listed are credit or debit card, PayPal and cryptocurrency.

reliability_note: a 7-day money-back guarantee applies, subject to the vendor's refund policy; no outage history was read.
confidence_note: the shape, the VND prices and the identity gate come from the vendor's own cart and sign-up pages; the USD price comes from the vendor's own forum post, because the cart's USD currency switch is a POST form that a plain read does not submit. A cart page read in USD would raise this to documented.
